phrases.arabic: أَيْنَ كُنْتَ؟ لِمَاذَا لَمْ تَأْتِ لِتُعَيِّدَ مَعَنَا؟
phrases.transliteration: ayna kunta? limaadha lam ta2ti li-tu3ayyida ma3anaa?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Blessed Eid, Salma.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيكَ. كُلُّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتَ بِخَيْر.
dialogue.transliteration: baaraka allaahu feeka. kullu 3aamin wa anta bikhayr.
dialogue.english: God bless you. May you be well every year.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَأَنْتِ بِخَيْر. هَلْ ذَهَبْتُمْ إِلَى صَلَاةِ الْعِيد؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa anti bikhayr. hal dhahabtum ilaa salaati al-3eed?
dialogue.english: And you. Did you go to the Eid prayer?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، ذَهَبْنَا صَبَاحًا، ثُمَّ زُرْنَا جَدَّتِي.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, dhahabnaa sabaa7an, thumma zurnaa jaddatee.
dialogue.english: Yes, we went in the morning, then visited my grandmother.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And did the children get their Eid money?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Yes, and they are very happy.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: Please, have some Eid cookies.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Thanks, they are delicious.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: May God bring it back to you in good health.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Amen. Blessed be the Eid upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: God bless you.

pair.english: May you be well every year.
Did you go to the Eid prayer?

response.english: Yes, we went in the morning.

pair.english: What did you eat at the Eid?
May God bring it back to you in good health.

lessons.culture: Eid greetings are exchanged in person and by message on the morning of the Eid, and Fusha phrases such as كُلُّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتَ بِخَيْر are understood in every Arab country. Children receive the الْعِيدِيَّة, a small gift of money, from relatives.

dialogue.english: Ramadan is generous, Hind.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: God is more generous. How is the fasting going?

dialogue.transliteration: al7amdu lillaah, na7nu saa2imoon wa bikhayr.
dialogue.english: Thank God, we are fasting and well.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: What time is iftar today?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: A little after six o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: We are preparing for iftar now.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: And do you have qatayef?

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: Yes, qatayef is a Ramadan sweet.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Whose invitation are you going to tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: To my uncle's house for iftar.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: May God accept your fasting.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: And from you. Blessed Ramadan.

lessons.culture: During Ramadan people greet each other with رَمَضَانُ كَرِيم, and families gather at sunset to break the fast together. The pre-dawn meal, the السُّحُور, is eaten before the call to the dawn prayer.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: مَبْرُوك يَا سَامِي، سَمِعْتُ خَبَرَ زَوَاجِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: mabrook yaa Saamee, sami3tu khabara zawaajika.
dialogue.english: Congratulations Sami, I heard the news of your wedding.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيكِ. سَنَحْتَفِلُ الْأُسْبُوعَ الْقَادِم.
dialogue.transliteration: baaraka allaahu feeki. sana7taflu al-usboo3a al-qaadim.
dialogue.english: God bless you. We will celebrate next week.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: When is the wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: On Friday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: Are you preparing for the wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Yes, the stage decoration is very beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: And who is invited to the wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Family and friends, everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: May God make you happy and bless you both.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Amen. And may it be your turn next.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: Thank you, see you at the wedding.

lessons.culture: At a wedding guests congratulate both families with phrases like مَبْرُوك and أَسْعَدَكُمُ اللهُ. The dabke is a line dance of the Levant that often opens the celebration, and bringing a gift is customary.

dialogue.english: Happy birthday, Mazen.

dialogue.speaker: Mazen
dialogue.english: Thank you, Nour.

dialogue.speaker: Nour

dialogue.speaker: Mazen
dialogue.english: I turned thirty.

dialogue.speaker: Nour

dialogue.speaker: Mazen
dialogue.english: And who is invited?

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.english: Family and friends. Blow out the candles.

dialogue.speaker: Mazen
dialogue.english: Amen. May you all be well every year.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.english: What gift do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Mazen
dialogue.english: I want a new book.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.english: May God lengthen your life.

dialogue.speaker: Mazen
dialogue.english: Amen. Thank you all.

lessons.culture: Birthdays are celebrated with a cake, candles and gifts, and the usual wish in Fusha is عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيد. Good news such as a success, a promotion or a new baby is met with مَبْرُوكٌ عَلَى followed by the news.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Congratulations on the newborn, Faisal.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: God bless you. Thank you for visiting.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: جَعَلَهُ اللهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِين. مَاذَا سَمَّيْتَهُ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ja3alahu allaahu mina as-saali7een. maadhaa sammaytahu?
dialogue.english: May God make him righteous. What did you name him?

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: We named him after his grandfather, Yusuf.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: اسْمٌ جَمِيل. أَنْبَتَهُ اللهُ نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا.
dialogue.english: A beautiful name. May God raise him well.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: Amen. Please, this is his cradle.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: He looks a lot like his father.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: So they say.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And how is the mother?

dialogue.speaker: Faisal

dialogue.english: Thank God, the mother and baby are safe.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: This is a gift for the baby.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: May God reward you well, Omar.

lessons.culture: A newborn is welcomed with مَبْرُوكٌ عَلَى الْمَوْلُود and a prayer that he grows up righteous, and the family often names him after a grandfather or a prophet. Visitors bring a small gift and call on the mother and baby in the first days.

dialogue.speaker: Sami

dialogue.speaker: Khalid

dialogue.speaker: Sami

dialogue.speaker: Sami

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: حَمْدًا لِلَّهِ عَلَى سَلَامَتِكُمْ يَا حَاجّ صَالِح.
dialogue.english: Thank God for your safe return, Haji Salih.

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.english: May God keep you safe.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: حَجٌّ مَبْرُورٌ وَسَعْيٌ مَشْكُورٌ وَذَنْبٌ مَغْفُور.
dialogue.transliteration: 7ajjun mabroorun wa sa3yun mashkoorun wa dhanbun maghfoor.
dialogue.english: An accepted Hajj, an appreciated effort and a forgiven sin.

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.english: God bless you. Please sit down.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: How did you find Makkah?

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.arabic: أَجْمَلُ أَيَّامِ حَيَاتِي. طُفْنَا حَوْلَ الْكَعْبَةِ وَبَكَيْتُ كَثِيرًا.
dialogue.transliteration: ajmalu ayyaami 7ayaatee. tufnaa 7awla al-ka3bati wa bakaytu katheeran.
dialogue.english: The best days of my life. We circled the Kaaba and I cried a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: And did you visit the Prophet's Mosque?

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ. وَأَحْضَرْتُ لَكُمْ تَمْرًا وَمَاءَ زَمْزَم.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am. wa a7dartu lakum tamran wa maa2a zamzam.
dialogue.english: Yes. And I brought you dates and zamzam water.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا. تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ مِنْك.
dialogue.transliteration: jazaaka allaahu khayran. taqabbala allaahu mink.
dialogue.english: May God reward you well. May God accept it from you.

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.english: From us and from you.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: May God grant us a visit to His house.

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.arabic: آمِين يَا رَبّ. إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تَزُورُهُ قَرِيبًا.
dialogue.transliteration: aameen yaa rabb. in shaa2a allaahu tazooruhu qareeban.
dialogue.english: Amen, O Lord. God willing, you will visit it soon.

response.english: The best days of my life.

pair.english: May God accept it from you.
May God grant us a visit to His house.

lessons.culture: A returning pilgrim is welcomed at home with حَجٌّ مَبْرُورٌ وَسَعْيٌ مَشْكُورٌ وَذَنْبٌ مَغْفُور and a prayer that God accept the Hajj. The pilgrim shares stories of Makkah and gives visitors zamzam water and dates, and the guest asks to be remembered in his prayers.

exercises.tip: Learn it as one block: a7dartu lakum tamran wa maa2a zamzam.

exercises.tip: hadhaa maa2u zamzam is the natural Fusha wording.

exercises.tip: Say the finished sentence aloud to check the order.

exercises.tip: sallamaka allaah is the usual answer.

phrases.transliteration: inna lillaahi wa inna ilayhi raaji3oon

reply.english: And may God give you good consolation.
Amen, may God reward you well.
No thanks are due for a duty.
In the cemetery near the mosque.
Yes, may God have mercy on him.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ يَا عُمَرُ. بَلَغَنِي خَبَرُ وَفَاةِ وَالِدِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: inna lillaahi wa inna ilayhi raaji3oon yaa 3umar. balaghanee khabaru wafaati waalidika.
dialogue.english: To God we belong and to Him we return, Omar. The news of your father's death reached me.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ. جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا عَلَى حُضُورِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: wa inna ilayhi raaji3oon. jazaaka allaahu khayran 3alaa HuDoorika.
dialogue.english: And to Him we return. May God reward you well for coming.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.english: May God magnify your reward and give you good consolation.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And may God be good to you.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.transliteration: raHimahu allaahu wa askanahu faseeHa jannaatihi.
dialogue.english: May God have mercy on him and house him in His spacious gardens.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Amen. He loved you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: كَانَ رَجُلًا طَيِّبًا، وَالْجَمِيعُ يَشْهَدُ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: kaana rajulan Tayyiban, wa al-jamee3u yashhadu lahu bi-dhaalika.
dialogue.english: He was a good man, and everyone bears witness to that.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: صَلَاةُ الْجَنَازَةِ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْكَبِيرِ.
dialogue.transliteration: Salaatu al-janaazati ba3da aZ-Zuhri fee al-masjidi al-kabeer.
dialogue.english: The funeral prayer is after the noon prayer in the big mosque.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: سَنَحْضُرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ. وَإِنِ احْتَجْتَ إِلَى شَيْءٍ فَأَنَا حَاضِرٌ.
dialogue.transliteration: sanaHDuru in shaa2a allaahu. wa ini aHtajta ilaa shay2in fa-ana HaaDir.
dialogue.english: We will attend, God willing. And if you need anything, I am here.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: May God reward your effort, Khaled.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: لَا شُكْرَ عَلَى وَاجِبٍ. أَلْهَمَكُمُ اللهُ الصَّبْرَ.
dialogue.transliteration: laa shukra 3alaa waajib. alhamakumu allaahu aS-Sabra.
dialogue.english: No thanks are due for a duty. May God grant you patience.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Amen, may God reward you well.

response.english: And may God give you good consolation.
No thanks are due for a duty.

pair.english: May God have mercy on him.

lessons.culture: Condolences open with إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ and are given at the family's home or after the funeral prayer, where the visitor keeps the words short and gentle. The burial is done quickly, so people attend the prayer and the burial to share the family's grief and are thanked with شَكَرَ اللهُ سَعْيَكُمْ.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'We belong to God and to Him we return'
accepted: inna lillaahi wa inna ilayhi raaji3oon
exercises.tip: It is said at once on hearing of a death; learn it as one block.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'May God have mercy on him'
exercises.tip: The verb comes first: raHima, then allaahu.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'May God magnify your reward'?
exercises.tip: ajr is the reward; 3azzama makes it great.

exercises.prompt: Which one answers 'شَكَرَ اللهُ سَعْيَكُمْ'?
exercises.tip: Attending is a duty, so no thanks are due.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'May God house him in His spacious gardens'
exercises.tip: The verb comes first, then God, then what He gives.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'We will attend the funeral, God willing'

too_formal.item: رح نحضر الجنازة إن شاء الله

exercises.tip: sa- before the verb makes it future.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'شَكَرَ اللهُ _____' (May God reward your effort)
exercises.tip: sa3y is the effort made to come.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أَتَقَدَّمُ إِلَى الْعَائِلَةِ بِخَالِصِ _____' (My sincere condolences to the family)
exercises.tip: at-ta3aazee is the plural: condolences.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'عَظَّمَ اللهُ أَجْرَكُمْ'. Reply naturally.
exercises.tip: The reply wishes them good consolation in return.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'مَتَى صَلَاةُ الْجَنَازَةِ؟'. Answer that it is after the noon prayer.
exercises.tip: Prayer times name the hour: Zuhr is the noon prayer.

phrases.arabic: لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
phrases.transliteration: laa ba2s, Tahoorun in shaa2a allaahu

reply.english: Amen, may God reward you well.

reply.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّنِي أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الرَّاحَةِ أُسْبُوعًا
reply.transliteration: qaala innanee aHtaaju ilaa ar-raaHati usboo3an
reply.english: He said I need a week of rest.
There was no need for the trouble, thank you.
How beautiful it is! Thank you.
On the contrary, your visit makes me happy.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا حَسَنُ. لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ.
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum yaa Hasan. laa ba2s, Tahoorun in shaa2a allaahu.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, Hassan. No harm, it is a purification, God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا عَلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. jazaaka allaahu khayran 3alaa az-ziyaara.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. May God reward you well for the visit.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: How are you feeling today?

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Praise God, better than before.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: What did the doctor say?

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّنِي سَأَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْمُسْتَشْفَى غَدًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ.
dialogue.transliteration: qaala innanee sa-akhruju mina al-mustashfaa ghadan in shaa2a allaahu.
dialogue.english: He said I will leave the hospital tomorrow, God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. أَحْضَرْتُ لَكَ بَعْضَ الْفَاكِهَةِ.
dialogue.transliteration: al-Hamdu lillaah. aHDartu laka ba3Da al-faakihati.
dialogue.english: Praise God. I brought you some fruit.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.arabic: لَا دَاعِيَ لِلتَّكَلُّفِ. شُكْرًا لَكَ يَا يُوسُفُ.
dialogue.transliteration: laa daa3iya lit-takalluf. shukran laka yaa yoosuf.
dialogue.english: There was no need for the trouble. Thank you, Yusuf.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: لَنْ أُطِيلَ عَلَيْكَ. اِرْتَحْ وَلَا تُتْعِبْ نَفْسَكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: lan uTeela 3alayka. irtaH wa laa tut3ib nafsaka.
dialogue.english: I won't stay long. Rest and don't tire yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: On the contrary, your visit makes me happy.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.transliteration: shafaaka allaahu yaa Hasan, wa salaamatuka.
dialogue.english: May God heal you, Hassan, and get well soon.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: Amen, God bless you.

pair.arabic: لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
pair.transliteration: laa ba2s, Tahoorun in shaa2a allaahu
pair.english: No harm, it is a purification, God willing.

response.english: Amen, may God reward you well.

lessons.culture: Visiting the sick is a recommended duty, and the visitor says لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ, words reported from the Prophet, peace be upon him, when he visited the ill. The visit is short so the patient can rest, and a gift of fruit or flowers is common.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'May God heal you'
exercises.tip: To a woman it becomes shafaaki.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I brought you some fruit'
exercises.tip: ba3D means some of; laka means for you (to a man).

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'No harm, it is a purification, God willing'?
options: لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
exercises.answer: لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
accepted: لَا بَأْسَ، طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
لا بأس، طهور إن شاء الله
laa ba2s, Tahoorun in shaa2a allaahu

too_formal.item: ما في شي، تطهير إن شاء الله

exercises.tip: Illness is seen as a cleansing, so this is said to comfort.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'How are you feeling today?'
exercises.tip: Haal is condition; -ka asks a man.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'When will you leave the hospital?'
exercises.tip: The question word comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Rest and don't tire yourself'
exercises.tip: laa before the verb forbids it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'مَاذَا قَالَ _____؟' (What did the doctor say?)
exercises.tip: aT-Tabeeb is the doctor.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'هَذِهِ بَاقَةُ _____ لَكَ' (This bouquet of flowers is for you)
exercises.tip: baaqatu wardin: a bunch of roses or flowers.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'شَفَاكَ اللهُ'. Reply naturally.
exercises.tip: Say aameen first, then thank him.

exercises.prompt: You are the patient and hear: 'كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْمَ؟'. Say you are better than before.
exercises.tip: Even when ill, begin with al-Hamdu lillaah.

phrases.transliteration: qaddara allaahu wa maa shaa2a fa3al

reply.english: Your standing by my side is enough for me.

phrases.arabic: أَنَا مَعَكَ فِي أَيِّ وَقْتٍ تَحْتَاجُنِي
phrases.transliteration: ana ma3aka fee ayyi waqtin taHtaajunee

reply.english: God will compensate you with something better.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: مَا بِكَ يَا بِلَالُ؟ وَجْهُكَ حَزِينٌ.
dialogue.transliteration: maa bika yaa bilaal? wajhuka Hazeen.
dialogue.english: What is wrong, Bilal? Your face is sad.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.english: I lost my job today.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا آسِفٌ جِدًّا لِهَذَا الْخَبَرِ. مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ana aasifun jiddan li-haadhaa al-khabar. maadhaa Hadatha?
dialogue.english: I am very sorry to hear this news. What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: أَغْلَقَتِ الشَّرِكَةُ فَرْعَهَا وَاسْتَغْنَتْ عَنْ عَدَدٍ مِنَ الْمُوَظَّفِينَ.
dialogue.transliteration: aghlaqat ash-sharikatu far3ahaa wa istaghnat 3an 3adadin mina al-muwaZZafeen.
dialogue.english: The company closed its branch and let go a number of employees.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: اِصْبِرْ يَا أَخِي، إِنَّ اللهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ.
dialogue.transliteration: iSbir yaa akhee, inna allaaha ma3a aS-Saabireen.
dialogue.english: Be patient, my brother, God is with the patient.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ، لَكِنَّنِي قَلِقٌ عَلَى أُسْرَتِي.
dialogue.transliteration: al-Hamdu lillaahi 3alaa kulli Haal, lakinnanee qaliqun 3alaa usratee.
dialogue.english: Praise God in every situation, but I am worried about my family.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: قَدَّرَ اللهُ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ. وَلَعَلَّ فِيهِ خَيْرًا لَكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: qaddara allaahu wa maa shaa2a fa3al. wa la3alla feehi khayran laka.
dialogue.english: God decreed, and what He wills He does. And perhaps there is good in it for you.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.english: God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: يَكْفِينِي وُقُوفُكَ بِجَانِبِي، وَإِنْ سَمِعْتَ عَنْ عَمَلٍ فَأَخْبِرْنِي.
dialogue.transliteration: yakfeenee wuqoofuka bi-jaanibee, wa in sami3ta 3an 3amalin fa-akhbirnee.
dialogue.english: Your standing by my side is enough, and if you hear of a job, tell me.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: سَأَسْأَلُ عَنْ فُرْصَةِ عَمَلٍ لَكَ، وَسَيُيَسِّرُ اللهُ لَكَ الْأَمْرَ.
dialogue.transliteration: sa-as2alu 3an furSati 3amalin laka, wa sa-yuyassiru allaahu laka al-amr.
dialogue.english: I will ask about a job opportunity for you, and God will make it easy for you.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.english: May God reward you well, Adel.

response.english: God will compensate you with something better.
Your standing by my side is enough for me.

lessons.culture: Comfort in hard times rests on sabr, patience, and on the belief that all things happen by God's decree, so a friend reminds gently and does not lecture. Offering real help, such as asking about a job opening or simply staying beside him, means more than long speeches.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Be patient, God is with the patient'
exercises.tip: The second half is from the Qur'an, 2:153.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'How can I help you?'
exercises.tip: an plus a verb gives 'to help': an usaa3idaka.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Everything is by God's decree'?
exercises.tip: qadar is what God has decreed.

exercises.prompt: Which one do you say to a friend who failed an exam?
exercises.tip: Comfort first, then point to the next try.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'God decreed, and what He wills He does'
accepted: qaddara allaahu wa maa shaa2a fa3al
exercises.tip: Said as one fixed saying, in this order.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'God will make it easy for you'
exercises.tip: sa- makes it future; the verb comes first.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'لَعَلَّ فِيهِ _____' (Perhaps there is good in it)
exercises.tip: After la3alla the noun takes -an.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'رَسَبْتُ فِي _____' (I failed the exam)
exercises.tip: al-imtiHaan is the exam; fee takes the -i ending.

exercises.prompt: A friend tells you: 'فَقَدْتُ وَظِيفَتِي الْيَوْمَ'. Comfort him.
exercises.tip: Remind him that God compensates.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِقَدَرِ اللهِ'. Reply naturally.
exercises.tip: Accepting the decree is answered with praise.

challenge.title: Celebrate with a friend
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you greet a friend at the Eid, congratulate them on a wedding or a success, wish someone a happy birthday, and ask what time iftar is.
required_elements: an Eid greeting and its reply
a question about the time of iftar
a prayer or blessing such as بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيك

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: Blessed Eid, Karim.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيكِ. كُلُّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتِ بِخَيْر.
dialogue.transliteration: baaraka allaahu feeki. kullu 3aamin wa anti bikhayr.
dialogue.english: God bless you. May you be well every year.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: Congratulations on the promotion.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Thank you. May God make you happy.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: Tomorrow is my sister's birthday.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Happy birthday to her from me.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. wa mataa maw3idu al-iftaari ghadan?
dialogue.english: Thanks. And what time is iftar tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: A little after six.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.english: May God accept your fasting.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: And from you. May God lengthen your life.
